To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Co2+ and lanthanum accelerate deactivation, slow inactivation and shift the voltage-dependence of activation to more positive values.
Co2+ (at concentrations previously reported to "block" IKr) and La3+, at concentrations previously reported to inhibit HERG channels, do not block HERG channels.
Co2+ and, especially, La3+ alter the gating of HERGs channels expressed in Xenopoulos oocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of Co2+ on the gating of HERGs channels, which are important for the normal repolarization process of cardiac action potential.
the effects of divalent and trivalents cations on the gating of the HERG potassium channel.
the molecular basis of cardiac repolarization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of Co2+ (and La3+) on the HERG channels are similar to that of Ca2+ but with a greater potency and a more pronounced shift of voltage dependence.
the effects of Co2+ (and La3+) on IHERG result from an acceleration in the deactivation kinetics, a slowing of inactivation, and a positive shift in voltage dependence of activation.
Co2+ and to a lesser extent, La3+, alter HERG channel gating by a mechanism similar to that of Ca2+.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Co2+ and Ca2+ are similar, but La3+ is different from these cations, with regard to their effects on HERG channels, and that these effects on the HERG channel are not consistent with a pore block mechanism.

Co2+ and other cations that are capable of binding to the S6 segment, such as Ca2+, shift the voltage dependence of HERG activation by interacting with a site on the S6 segment that is distinct from the pore region.
the divalent and trivalents ions (Co2+ and La2+) affect the gating of the HERG channels, and not the permeation of the ions through the channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of Co2+ (and La3+) on HERG are not due to pore block, but rather to altered channel gating.
the effects of Co2+ on HERGs are more complex than previously thought and that the effects are not consistent with the effects of Ca.
the effects of divalent cations on HERG gating are complex and cannot simply be interpreted as block of the pore.
